title: Standard Costing
outcomes: Explain standards and the purpose of variance analysis.

meta.exam_tip: Compute the total variance first, then sub-variances, and show that they reconcile.

concepts.title: Standards, standard costing and variance analysis
body: A standard is a predetermined measure of what cost should be under efficient conditions; standard costing compares actual costs with standards, finds variances, and analyses causes for corrective action.
Types of standards: ideal (perfect conditions), basic (unchanged long-term base), currently attainable (achievable with efficient effort — most useful), and normal (average over a cycle).
Setting standards needs input from purchasing (prices), engineering (quantities, times), HR (wage rates) and accounts (overhead rates), usually summarised on a standard cost card.
Variance = standard cost of actual output − actual cost; favourable when actual is lower, adverse when higher. Variances help apply management by exception.
concepts.analogy: Standards are the "should" against which the "did" is measured.
concepts.work: If standard material per chair is ₹500 and actual is ₹540, the ₹40 adverse variance triggers a check on price and usage.

concepts.title: Material and labour variances
body: Material: cost variance = SQ × SP − AQ × AP; price variance = AQ × (SP − AP) (on purchase or on usage); usage variance = SP × (SQ − AQ), which splits into mix variance = SP × (revised SQ − AQ) and yield variance = SP × (SQ − revised SQ) when several materials are mixed.

Labour: cost variance = SH × SR − AH paid × AR; rate variance = AH paid × (SR − AR); idle time variance = idle hours × SR (always adverse); efficiency variance = SR × (SH − AH worked), which can be split into mix (gang) and yield (sub-efficiency) variances.
Causes: price — market changes, poor buying; usage — wastage, poor quality material; rate — wage revisions, wrong grade; efficiency — poor supervision, machine breakdown, untrained staff.
concepts.analogy: Every variance splits into a price effect and a quantity effect.
concepts.work: Buying cheaper but poorer material can give a favourable price variance and an adverse usage variance.

concepts.title: Overhead and sales variances
body: Variable overheads: cost variance = standard VOH for actual output − actual VOH; expenditure variance = AH × standard rate − actual VOH; efficiency variance = standard rate × (SH − AH).

Fixed overheads: cost variance = absorbed (actual output × standard rate per unit) − actual; expenditure (budget) variance = budgeted − actual; volume variance = absorbed − budgeted, which splits into capacity, efficiency and calendar variances when hours are used.

Sales variances (turnover or margin basis): sales price variance = AQ × (AP − SP); sales volume variance = SP (or standard margin) × (AQ − BQ), splitting into mix and quantity variances for multiple products.
concepts.analogy: Overhead variances separate overspending from under-use of capacity.
concepts.work: Producing 1,000 units against a 1,200-unit budget leaves fixed overheads under-absorbed — an adverse volume variance.

concepts.title: Reporting and controlling variances
body: Variances are reported regularly to the managers responsible — purchase manager for price, production manager for usage and efficiency.
Not all variances are controllable; uncontrollable ones (e.g. a statutory wage increase) may call for revising standards.

Advantages of standard costing: cost control, efficient pricing, budgeting support, simpler stock valuation; limitations: cost of setting standards, standards becoming outdated, and possible demotivation if standards are unrealistic.
concepts.analogy: Variance analysis is valuable only if someone acts on it.
concepts.work: A recurring adverse labour efficiency variance points to training or equipment problems.

illustrations.title: Where did the cost go?
illustrations.q: Standard per unit: 2 kg of material at ₹50/kg; 3 labour hours at ₹100/hour. Actual output 1,000 units used 2,100 kg bought at ₹48/kg; workers were paid for 3,300 hours at ₹95/hour, of which 100 hours were idle due to a power failure. Compute material and labour variances.

illustrations.title: Fixed overheads
illustrations.q: Budgeted fixed overheads ₹2,40,000 for 1,200 units (₹200 per unit). Actual fixed overheads ₹2,50,000; actual output 1,000 units. Compute the fixed overhead cost, expenditure and volume variances.

jobs.title: Monthly variance report
jobs.situation: The plant head wants a one-page explanation of why actual cost exceeded standard.
steps: Compute material, labour and overhead variances.
Assign each to a responsible manager.
jobs.takeaway: Reconcile totals first — a variance report that does not add up loses credibility.

mcqs.q: The most useful standard for control is:
mcqs.explain: Attainable standards are achievable with efficient effort, motivating staff while revealing real inefficiency. In practice: review them periodically.
mcqs.topic: Standards, standard costing and variance analysis

mcqs.q: AQ 500 kg at ₹22; SP ₹20. Material price variance:
mcqs.explain: 500 × (20 − 22) = −1,000: adverse. In practice: check supplier prices.

mcqs.q: SQ 1,000 kg, AQ 950 kg, SP ₹10. Usage variance:
mcqs.explain: 10 × (1,000 − 950) = ₹500 F. In practice: may reflect better material quality.
Paid hours not worked cost money with no output. In practice: separate normal idle time in the standard.

mcqs.q: SH 2,000; AH worked 2,200; SR ₹50. Labour efficiency variance:
Fixed overhead volume variance arises from:
options: Difference between actual and budgeted output
mcqs.explain: It is absorbed minus budgeted fixed overheads, due to output differing from budget. In practice: it reflects capacity use.
Spent less than budget: favourable. In practice: check whether savings are sustainable.

mcqs.q: Actual 900 units sold at ₹105 vs standard price ₹100. Sales price variance:
mcqs.explain: 900 × (105 − 100) = 4,500 F. In practice: volume variance is separate.

questions.q: Standard per unit: 2 kg of material at ₹50/kg; 3 labour hours at ₹100/hour. Actual output 1,000 units used 2,100 kg bought at ₹48/kg; workers were paid for 3,300 hours at ₹95/hour, of which 100 hours were idle due to a power failure. Compute material and labour variances.
Budgeted fixed overheads ₹2,40,000 for 1,200 units (₹200 per unit). Actual fixed overheads ₹2,50,000; actual output 1,000 units. Compute the fixed overhead cost, expenditure and volume variances.

summary: MCV = SQ·SP − AQ·AP; MPV = AQ(SP − AP); MUV = SP(SQ − AQ).
LCV = SH·SR − AH·AR; LRV = AH paid(SR − AR); idle = idle hrs × SR; LEV = SR(SH − AH worked).
FOH: expenditure = budget − actual; volume = absorbed − budget.
Sales price = AQ(AP − SP); volume = SP(AQ − BQ).
remember: Standard quantity is for actual output.
traps: Idle time variance is always adverse.

viva.model: A technique that sets predetermined costs, compares actual costs with them, analyses the variances and takes corrective action.

viva.q: How is material usage variance computed?
viva.model: Standard price multiplied by the difference between standard quantity for actual output and actual quantity used.
Because paying for hours not worked has different causes, such as power failure, from inefficiency in hours actually worked.

viva.q: What does fixed overhead volume variance show?
viva.model: The over- or under-absorption of fixed overheads because actual output differs from budgeted output.

viva.q: Name two limitations of standard costing.
viva.model: Standards are costly to set and may become outdated; unrealistic standards can demotivate staff.

cases.title: Crisp Snacks
cases.case: Crisp Snacks: standard for one packet — 0.5 kg potato at ₹30/kg. In March it made 4,000 packets using 2,100 kg bought at ₹28/kg. Standard labour 0.1 hour at ₹120; actual 420 hours at ₹125.

mcqs.explain: SQ 2,000 kg; 30 × (2,000 − 2,100) = 3,000 A. In practice: check peeling wastage.
420 × (120 − 125) = 2,100 A. In practice: overtime may explain it.
SH 400; 120 × (400 − 420) = 2,400 A. In practice: total labour variance ₹4,500 A.
